root_cause_analysis.root_cause: In pytest 6.1.0 the Collector.collect implementation was changed to call the underlying path‑listing API with `follow_symlinks=False`. This causes directories that are symbolic links to be ignored during test discovery, whereas previously they were traversed like normal directories.
root_cause_analysis.behavioral_contract: The pytest collection system must treat a directory symlink as a regular directory and descend into it to discover test modules, unless the user explicitly disables following symlinks via configuration. Collector.collect (and its subclasses Module.collect and Package.collect) must therefore follow symlinks when walking the filesystem.
root_cause_analysis.expected_behavior: When a test root contains a symlink that points to another directory containing test files, pytest should discover and collect those test files exactly as if the directory were present directly in the tree.
root_cause_analysis.current_behavior: Because `follow_symlinks=False` is passed during directory traversal, pytest skips over symlinked directories entirely, resulting in the tests inside those directories not being collected.
relevant_tests: testing/test_pathlib.py (indirectly, via bestrelpath handling of symlinks)
any test that creates a temporary directory, symlinks it into the test tree and asserts that its tests are run
root_cause_analysis.required_change: Remove the explicit `follow_symlinks=False` argument (or change it to `True`) in the directory‑listing call inside `Collector.collect` so that symlinked directories are traversed. Ensure the default behavior matches the pre‑6.1.0 version, i.e., follow symlinks unless the user opts out.
regression_risks: Introducing infinite recursion when a symlink creates a cycle (e.g., a directory symlinks to one of its ancestors). The collector must guard against revisiting already visited real paths.
Potential duplicate collection of the same test module if multiple symlinks point to the same directory; deduplication logic may be needed.
Changing the default may affect users who relied on the newer behaviour of ignoring symlinks; ensure that an explicit configuration option (e.g., `--no-follow-symlinks`) can still suppress following.
Performance impact on very large directory trees with many symlinks, though likely negligible.
